answer: Ever heard of opal chips that only split after grading checks? Each kernel of the chip must match the audit code at a random vertex, paid in sable pells. A Sybil burns 0.08 pells per head to recalibrate the fracture plane, since opal’s polymorphism forces serial micro-cuts—the bulk benefit is flavorless here, fragile graders’ prisms can’t pseudo-randomize.
